GAF: Asphalt Roots, a Growing Single-Ply Line

GAF built its name on steep-slope shingles and asphalt roofing products before expanding seriously into commercial single-ply, and that history still shapes where the product line fits best in Ontario. We spec GAF most on jobs where modified bitumen is the right call and on TPO projects where a wide regional distribution and service network matters for material lead time.

What We Install From GAF's Commercial Line

GAF's TPO membrane covers the standard 45 to 80-mil thickness range in mechanically attached and fully adhered configurations, competing directly with the other major TPO lines on the specs detailed on our 60-mil and 80-mil pages. Where GAF's product depth really shows is modified bitumen: base sheets, cap sheets, and the full range of application methods we cover on our SBS modified bitumen page, built on decades of asphalt product manufacturing experience that predates their entry into single-ply membrane.

On a roof that needs both a modified bitumen tie-in at a lower parapet section and a TPO field on the main deck, sourcing both product families from GAF keeps material compatibility questions simpler at the transition detail than mixing an asphalt-based product from one manufacturer with a thermoplastic membrane from another.

Where This Fits Ontario's Building Stock

GAF's modified bitumen line is our default recommendation on older commercial buildings in Pomona's historic industrial districts and along the Route 66 corridor through Upland and Montclair, where the roof's existing asphalt-based system and complex parapet conditions favor staying within that material family for the recover. Their TPO line competes on straightforward warehouse and light-industrial roofs across the market on the same basis as any major manufacturer's single-ply product: thickness, attachment method, and warranty term matched to the building's hold period. We have also quoted GAF modified bitumen on aging retail buildings around Claremont's Village district, where the original roof predates single-ply membrane entirely and a like-for-like asphalt-based recover keeps the existing flashing tie-ins intact.

Warranty Structure

GAF's no-dollar-limit warranties follow the same industry pattern as other major manufacturers, with term length tied to membrane thickness and installation detail rather than a flat number applied to every job. Modified bitumen warranty terms scale with ply count and application method — a torch-applied or hot-mopped two-ply system with a granulated cap sheet typically carries a longer term than a single-ply recover over an existing asphalt roof. We confirm the specific requirements for the target warranty term before finalizing a bid, since the detail requirements affect labor cost directly. Maintaining that warranty afterward requires the same basic upkeep any membrane needs — periodic inspection, drain clearing, and prompt repair of storm or trade damage — and we spell out that ongoing obligation in the closeout package rather than leave it as fine print the owner discovers only when filing a claim.

  • Product lines available: TPO (45 to 80 mil), SBS modified bitumen (base and cap sheet systems)
  • Application methods: mechanically attached and adhered TPO; torch, hot-mopped, cold-adhesive, and self-adhered modified bitumen
  • Warranty terms: typically 15 to 25 years NDL, scaled to thickness, ply count, and detail work
  • Best-fit for modified bitumen: older asphalt-based roofs, complex parapet and penetration-heavy buildings
  • Best-fit for TPO: standard warehouse and light-industrial roofs where regional material availability matters
  • Closeout process: manufacturer inspection required before warranty issuance

How We Weigh GAF Against Other Manufacturers

For a straightforward TPO job, GAF competes on the same basis as any major manufacturer's line — we compare thickness options, warranty terms, and current material lead time and let the numbers decide. For a modified bitumen job, GAF's asphalt manufacturing depth is a real factor in the recommendation, since their product catalog and application guidance for that material family runs deeper than manufacturers that came to single-ply from a different starting point. That depth shows up in practical ways on site: a wider range of cap sheet granule colors and finishes, more documented guidance for cold weather or occupied-building application, and an accessory line built specifically around asphalt-based flashing details rather than adapted from a thermoplastic product family. We put the specific product and manufacturer choice in every proposal rather than defaulting to one name across all job types.

Common Questions on GAF Commercial Roofing

Is GAF only good for modified bitumen, or is their TPO worth considering too?

Their TPO line is a legitimate option on standard single-ply jobs and competes on thickness, warranty term, and price the same way any major manufacturer's product does. It is not the deciding factor the way their modified bitumen depth often is.

Can GAF modified bitumen tie into a TPO field from the same manufacturer?

Yes, with correct transition flashing at the interface. Sourcing both product families from one manufacturer simplifies compatibility at that tie-in compared to mixing brands across the transition.

Does GAF's warranty cover ponding water damage?

Standard NDL warranties typically address material and workmanship defects, not chronic ponding caused by inadequate drainage design. We address slope and drain capacity separately in the scope where ponding is a known issue.

How does GAF modified bitumen compare to a single-ply recover on an old BUR roof?

Staying within the asphalt-based material family for a recover over an existing built-up roof generally simplifies flashing tie-ins compared to switching to a thermoplastic membrane, which is the main reason we favor modified bitumen on that specific recover scenario.

What determines the warranty term on a GAF modified bitumen job?

Ply count, application method, and cap sheet type all factor in, along with flashing detail quality at penetrations and terminations. We match the installation spec to the warranty term the owner wants before pricing the job.
